name.text: Graphing a feasible region for a textile workshop

questiontext.text:
A local textile workshop produces two types of high-quality garments: kitenge and kikoi. Let \( x \) represent the number of kitenge bolts and \( y \) represent the number of kikoi bolts produced per week.

  • Each bolt of kitenge requires {@A@} meters of raw material and {@D@} hours of labor.
  • Each bolt of kikoi requires {@B@} meters of raw material and {@E@} hours of labor.
  • The workshop has a maximum of {@C@} meters of raw material and {@F@} hours of labor available per week.

a) Algebraic Constraints:

Formulate the two linear inequalities that model the structural limitations of the workshop. (Use \( \le \) for "maximum of". Do not include the non-negativity constraints \(x \ge 0, y \ge 0\) in your answers below.)

Raw material constraint: [[input:ans1]]

Labor time constraint: [[input:ans2]]

Material check: [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
Labor check: [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

b) Graphical Representation:

Graph the feasible production region on the Cartesian plane below:

  • Drag the two blue points to set the boundary line for the raw material constraint.
  • Drag the two red points to set the boundary line for the labor time constraint.
  • Drag the green Region Marker into the overlapping feasible area that satisfies all constraints simultaneously (including \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: Algebraic Constraints

We translate the word problem into mathematical inequalities. For the raw material, kitenge uses \({@A@}\)m and kikoi uses \({@B@}\)m. The total cannot exceed \({@C@}\)m:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{{@A@}x + {@B@}y \le {@C@}} \)

For the labor time, kitenge uses \({@D@}\)h and kikoi uses \({@E@}\)h. The total cannot exceed \({@F@}\)h:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{{@D@}x + {@E@}y \le {@F@}} \)

Part b: Graphical Representation

To graph these inequalities, we find the axes intercepts for each boundary equation.

For the Material line (\( {@A@}x + {@B@}y = {@C@} \)):

  • Set \(x = 0 \implies {@B@}y = {@C@} \implies y = {@C/B@}\). Intercept: \((0, {@C/B@})\)
  • Set \(y = 0 \implies {@A@}x = {@C@} \implies x = {@C/A@}\). Intercept: \(({@C/A@}, 0)\)

For the Labor line (\( {@D@}x + {@E@}y = {@F@} \)):

  • Set \(x = 0 \implies {@E@}y = {@F@} \implies y = {@F/E@}\). Intercept: \((0, {@F/E@})\)
  • Set \(y = 0 \implies {@D@}x = {@F@} \implies x = {@F/D@}\). Intercept: \(({@F/D@}, 0)\)

We plot both solid lines. The feasible production region is the area bounded by both lines and the positive axes (\(x \ge 0, y \ge 0\)), as shown by the shaded region below.

[[jsxgraph width="400px" height="400px"]] var a_val = {#A#}; var b_val = {#B#}; var c_val = {#C#}; var d_val = {#D#}; var e_val = {#E#}; var f_val = {#F#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-2.5, 18.5, 18.5, -2.5], axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false} }); var xaxis = brd.create('axis', [[0, 0], [1, 0]], { name: 'x', withLabel: true, label: {position: 'rt', offset: [-15, 20]}, firstArrow: true, lastArrow: true, strokeWidth: 2, ticks: { drawLabels: true, label: {offset: [-8, -15]}, drawZero: true, insertTicks: false, ticksDistance: 2, minorTicks: 1, majorHeight: -1, minorHeight: -1, strokeColor: '#a0a0a0', strokeOpacity: 0.5, strokeWidth: 1, minorStrokeColor: '#e0e0e0', minorStrokeOpacity: 0.5, minorStrokeWidth: 1 } }); var yaxis = brd.create('axis', [[0, 0], [0, 1]], { name: 'y', withLabel: true, label: {position: 'rt', offset: [15, -15]}, firstArrow: true, lastArrow: true, strokeWidth: 2, ticks: { drawLabels: true, label: {offset: [-25, -5]}, drawZero: false, insertTicks: false, ticksDistance: 2, minorTicks: 1, majorHeight: -1, minorHeight: -1, strokeColor: '#a0a0a0', strokeOpacity: 0.5, strokeWidth: 1, minorStrokeColor: '#e0e0e0', minorStrokeOpacity: 0.5, minorStrokeWidth: 1 } }); /* Draw the boundary lines */ var p1_ws = brd.create('point', [0, c_val/b_val], {visible: false}); var p2_ws = brd.create('point', [c_val/a_val, 0], {visible: false}); var line1_ws = brd.create('line', [p1_ws, p2_ws], {strokeWidth: 3, strokeColor: '#1565c0', dash: 0}); var p3_ws = brd.create('point', [0, f_val/e_val], {visible: false}); var p4_ws = brd.create('point', [f_val/d_val, 0], {visible: false}); var line2_ws = brd.create('line', [p3_ws, p4_ws], {strokeWidth: 3, strokeColor: '#c62828', dash: 0}); /* Evaluate coordinates for the polygonal intersection to cleanly shade the feasible region */ var int_x = (c_val * e_val - b_val * f_val) / (a_val * e_val - b_val * d_val); var int_y = (a_val * f_val - c_val * d_val) / (a_val * e_val - b_val * d_val); var poly_p1 = brd.create('point', [0, 0], {visible: false}); var poly_p2 = brd.create('point', [Math.min(c_val/a_val, f_val/d_val), 0], {visible: false}); var poly_p3 = brd.create('point', [int_x, int_y], {visible: false}); var poly_p4 = brd.create('point', [0, Math.min(c_val/b_val, f_val/e_val)], {visible: false}); brd.create('polygon', [poly_p1, poly_p2, poly_p3, poly_p4], { fillColor: '#4caf50', fillOpacity: 0.3, borders: {strokeWidth: 0} }); /* Marker */ brd.create('point', [1, 1], {name: 'Feasible Region', size: 6, strokeColor: '#2e7d32', fillColor: '#4caf50', fixed: true}); [[/jsxgraph]]
